stops.title: Electrolytes, Acids-Bases & Ostwald's dilution law
stops.inShort: Bronsted-Lowry: acid = H⁺ donor, base = H⁺ acceptor (conjugate acid-base pair differs by one H⁺). Lewis: acid = e⁻ pair acceptor, base = e⁻ pair donor. Ostwald's dilution law for weak acid/base: K_a = α² c / (1 − α) ≈ α² c ⇒ α = √(K_a / c).

stops.title: Autoionization of water, pH & pOH
stops.inShort: Ionic product of water K_w = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻] = 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 298 K. pH = −log₁₀[H₃O⁺], pOH = −log₁₀[OH⁻], and pH + pOH = 14.

stops.title: Hydrolysis of salts & Buffer solutions
stops.inShort: Strong acid + strong base salt: neutral (pH 7); weak acid + strong base: basic (pH > 7); strong acid + weak base: acidic (pH < 7). Buffers resist pH change on small acid/base addition (e.g. CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa).

stops.title: Solubility product & Common ion effect
stops.inShort: For A_x B_y(s) ⇌ x A^(y+) + y B^(x−), K_sp = x^x y^y S^(x+y). Precipitation occurs when Ionic Product (IP) > K_sp. Common ion effect suppresses ionization of weak electrolyte.

board.text: Which formula co-relates degree of dissociation and concentration of electrolyte?
Define conjugate acid-base pair. The hydroxyl ion concentration in aqueous solution of NaOH is 2 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³. Calculate pH of the solution.
board.answer:
Conjugate acid-base pair: A pair of an acid and a base differing by a single proton (H⁺).
Given: [OH⁻] = 2 × 10⁻⁴ M.
pOH = −log₁₀(2 × 10⁻⁴) = 4 − log₁₀(2) = 4 − 0.3010 = 3.699.
pH = 14 − pOH = 14 − 3.699 = 10.301.

board.text: The pH of 0.001 M HCl solution is ____.
Explain buffer action of sodium acetate-acetic acid buffer.
board.answer:
Sodium acetate-acetic acid buffer contains large reservoirs of undissociated CH₃COOH and CH₃COO⁻ ions.
1. On adding a small amount of acid (H⁺): CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ → CH₃COOH (added H⁺ is removed, pH remains constant).
2. On adding a small amount of base (OH⁻): CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O (added OH⁻ is neutralized, pH remains constant).

Reaction on addition of small base (CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O)

board.text: Define acids and bases according to Bronsted-Lowry theory. Derive relationship between pH and pOH.
board.answer:
Bronsted-Lowry: Acid is a proton (H⁺) donor; Base is a proton (H⁺) acceptor.
Derivation: Ionic product of water at 298 K is K_w = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻] = 1 × 10⁻¹⁴.
Taking −log₁₀ on both sides:
−log₁₀[H₃O⁺] − log₁₀[OH⁻] = −log₁₀(10⁻¹⁴)
⇒ pH + pOH = 14.
